task.title: Slow Wi-Fi
task.shortdesc: Identify and correct conditions that reduce Wi-Fi performance on one or more client devices.

prereq.p: Before you troubleshoot slow Wi-Fi, make sure that:

ul.li: The or Optical Network Terminal (ONT) is connected to the ISP service.
The is turned on and connected to the Internet.
The affected client device is connected to .
The client device has Internet access.
You have recorded recent changes to the router, client device, or network environment.

prereq.note: Make one change at a time. Test Wi-Fi performance after each change.

context.p: Wi-Fi performance depends on the Internet service, router placement, distance, physical obstructions, interference, Wi-Fi band, network activity, and client-device capabilities.
A slow Internet service can appear to be a Wi-Fi problem. Compare a wired connection with a wireless connection before you change the Wi-Fi configuration.
context.note: Network speed can decrease when many devices stream video, download files, or use online applications at the same time.
Use the same test server, client device, test location, and network conditions when you compare performance results.

step.cmd: Determine which client devices have slow Wi-Fi.

substep.cmd: Test the Wi-Fi connection on another client device.
Test the devices from the same location.
Confirm whether the problem occurs on one device or on all wireless devices.

ul.li: If only one device is affected, check the device software, Wi-Fi adapter, and network settings.
If all wireless devices are affected, check the router, Internet service, interference, and network activity.
If the problem occurs only in one location, check the signal strength, distance, and physical obstructions.

step.cmd: Check the Internet service status.

info.p: Check whether the ISP has reported a service interruption or reduced service performance.
If the ISP reports a service problem, wait until the ISP restores normal service.

step.cmd: Compare the wired and wireless connections.

substep.cmd: Connect a computer to an available LAN port on the by using an Ethernet cable.
Stop unnecessary downloads, uploads, and streaming activities on other client devices.
Test the Internet connection on the wired computer.
Test the Wi-Fi connection from the same area.
Compare the results.

ul.li: If both connections are slow, check the ISP service, modem or ONT, router load, and Internet service plan.
If only the Wi-Fi connection is slow, continue to check the wireless connection.

info.note: Test results can be lower than the maximum rate specified by the ISP or Wi-Fi standard.

step.cmd: Check the Wi-Fi signal strength on the affected device.

substep.cmd: Move the client device closer to the .
Test Wi-Fi performance again.

info.p: If performance improves near the router, distance or a physical obstruction can be the cause of the problem.
Put the router in a central, open, and elevated location.

step.stepresult: The test determines whether the problem is related to distance or Wi-Fi signal strength.

step.cmd: Check the location of the router.

info.p: Make sure that the router is:

ul.li: In an open and elevated location
Near the center of the required coverage area
Outside a closed cabinet or drawer
Away from equipment that can cause interference

info.p: For more information, see .

step.cmd: Reduce physical obstructions between the router and the affected client device.

info.p: Walls, floors, metal objects, large appliances, mirrors, and water can weaken or reflect Wi-Fi signals.
Move the router or client device to provide a clearer signal path.

step.cmd: Check for sources of wireless interference.

info.note: A nearby device does not always cause interference. Test the connection before and after you move or turn off the device.

info.p: Move the router and client device away from the following equipment:
Test Wi-Fi performance after you move the router or potential source of interference.
For more information, see .

step.cmd: Test the client device on another Wi-Fi band.

choices.choice: Use the 5 GHz band for a compatible device that is near the router and requires higher network performance.
Use the 2.4 GHz band for a device that is far from the router or behind several physical obstructions.

step.cmd: Check the network for high-bandwidth activity.

info.p: Review the connected devices on the .
Look for activities such as:
Temporarily stop unnecessary network activity. Then, test Wi-Fi performance again.
info.note: Do not block a device until you confirm that the device is not authorized.

step.cmd: Check for unknown connected devices.

substep.cmd: Sign in to the .
Open the .
Review the list of connected devices.
Compare each device name or MAC address with your known devices.
Block a device only if you confirm that the device is not authorized.

info.note: Some client devices use private or randomized MAC addresses. Verify the address in the device network settings before you block the device.

step.cmd: Restart the affected client device.

info.p: Reconnect the device to after the restart.

step.cmd: Restart the router if the problem continues.

substep.cmd: Use the restart control in the if it is available.
Wait until the router status indicators show normal operation.
Reconnect the affected client device.
Test Wi-Fi performance again.

info.note: Do not press the reset button. A factory reset can remove the custom network configuration.

step.cmd: Check for an approved firmware update for the .

info.p: Use the firmware update function in the or get approved firmware from the .
info.note: Do not turn off the router during a firmware update.
Install only firmware intended for and the applicable .

step.cmd: Check for updates for the affected client device.

info.p: Install approved operating-system, Wi-Fi adapter, and device firmware updates.
info.note: Restart the client device if the update procedure requires a restart.

step.cmd: Review the Wi-Fi connection information.

info.p: Review the following information when available:

ul.li: Connected access point or mesh node

info.note: The negotiated Wi-Fi connection rate is not the same as the application data-transfer rate or Internet speed.

step.cmd: Review wireless channel utilization.

info.p: Use a wireless analysis tool or the available controls in the to identify nearby networks and busy channels.
Keep automatic channel selection enabled when wireless conditions change frequently.
If manual channel selection is necessary, use a permitted channel with low utilization.
info.note: Do not use in every environment without evaluating local wireless conditions and applicable regional requirements.

step.cmd: Review the configured channel width.

info.p: The default 5 GHz configuration in this guide uses .
A wide channel can support higher data rates when the wireless environment is clear. A narrower channel can provide a more stable connection in a congested environment.
info.note: Change the channel width only after you measure the wireless conditions. Test the network after the change.

step.cmd: Review traffic-priority settings if they are available.

info.p: Confirm that traffic-priority or Quality of Service settings do not incorrectly limit the affected device or application.
Prioritize delay-sensitive traffic only when network requirements justify the change.
info.note: Incorrect traffic-priority settings can reduce performance for other devices or applications.

step.cmd: Check the access point or mesh connection if the affected device does not connect directly to the main router.

info.p: Confirm that the or has a reliable connection to the network.
Move a wireless mesh node closer to the main router or another connected node if the backhaul connection is weak.
info.note: Use a wired backhaul connection when possible. A wired backhaul can provide more consistent performance than a shared wireless backhaul.
info.p: For more information, see .

step.cmd: Test Wi-Fi performance again.

substep.cmd: Stop unnecessary network activity.
Put the test device in its normal use location.
Connect the device to the required Wi-Fi band.
Run the same performance test again.
Compare the result with the initial result.

info.note: Record throughput, latency, packet loss, signal strength, band, channel, and channel width. Use the same test conditions for each comparison.

step.stepresult: The test confirms whether Wi-Fi performance has improved.

result.p: The affected client devices have a stable Wi-Fi connection and provide acceptable performance for the required network activities.

postreq.p: If Wi-Fi remains slow in a specific area, review the router location and consider the or to extend coverage.
If wired and wireless connections remain slow, contact the ISP to verify the Internet service.
If the problem continues, collect the following information:

ul.li: The wired and wireless test results
The Wi-Fi band and signal strength
The time when the problem occurs

postreq.note: Do not send Wi-Fi passwords, administrator passwords, account passwords, or other confidential credentials to technical support.
